entry.gloss: writing down a melody you hear
entry.def: Writing down a melody from hearing it, with its pitches and rhythm. A common method is to memorize the melody, find its tonic and meter, then write the rhythm and the scale degrees.

entry.gloss: writing down a rhythm you hear
entry.def: Writing down the rhythm of a passage from hearing it, in a given meter. Feeling the beat and counting its divisions helps to place each note.

entry.gloss: writing down a chord progression you hear
entry.def: Writing down a chord progression from hearing it, usually the bass line, the soprano and the Roman numerals. Hearing the bass line as scale degrees is the usual first step, since it narrows down the possible chords.

entry.gloss: singing music from notation at first sight
entry.def: Singing a melody from notation without having heard it first, usually with solfège syllables or scale-degree numbers. It trains the same link between notation and sound that dictation trains in the other direction.

entry.gloss: singing with the syllables do, re, mi
entry.def: Singing with the syllables do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti for the degrees of the scale (te in British tonic sol-fa, si in many other countries), and the ear-training and reading lessons built on them. Also called solfeggio, or sol-fa in British English. The syllables name the scale degrees in movable do and the note names in fixed do.

entry.gloss: do is the tonic of whatever key
entry.def: A solfège system in which do is the tonic of the current key, so each syllable stands for a scale degree: in G major, do is G and ti is F#. It is widely used in English-speaking countries and in the Kodály method; Curwen's tonic sol-fa is a form of it.

entry.gloss: do is always the note C
entry.def: A solfège system in which do is always C, re always D and so on, whatever the key and accidental, so the syllables are note names. It is the usual system in countries where the syllables are the note names, such as France, Italy and Spain.

entry.gloss: minor tonic sung as do, with me, le, te
entry.def: A movable-do practice in which the tonic of a minor key is do, as in major, and the lowered third, sixth and seventh degrees are sung me, le and te. It keeps one syllable per scale degree in both modes.

entry.gloss: minor tonic sung as la, as in the relative major
entry.def: A movable-do practice in which the tonic of a minor key is la, the syllable it has in the relative major; the raised seventh degree becomes si and the raised sixth fi. It is used in the Kodály method.

entry.gloss: degrees sung or written as 1 to 7
entry.def: Numbers from 1 to 7 for the scale degrees, counted from the tonic and written with a caret above them in analysis. Sung instead of solfège syllables, they work like movable do and fit any language.
